item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find credible 2024 evidence of large-scale political violence, communal violence, or protest crackdowns in Japan under Kishida. The evidence base instead centers on disaster response, rights protection, and the persistence of structural criminal-justice abuse. That means the main negative side is not state terror or mass repression, but unfinished institutional harm in detention and prosecution.","evidence":[{"title":"Instructions by the Prime Minister Regarding the Earthquake Centered in Ishikawa Prefecture","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 1, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/decisions/2024/0101shiji.html","summary":"Kishida ordered timely public warnings, evacuation, damage prevention, and emergency disaster response with human life first. This is strong evidence of safety-oriented crisis management.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7","3B.9"]},{"title":"Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the Package of Measures to Support the Daily Lives and the Livelihoods of the Disaster Victims and Other Matters","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 25, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the government had shifted from immediate response to restoring infrastructure and “peaceful livelihoods” for disaster victims. That supports a finding that he worked to reduce displacement and lingering insecurity after the quake.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.9"]},{"title":"People feeling safe and well-assured in their daily lives","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024 page content","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/safety.html","summary":"The cabinet’s own policy summary says the government’s mission is to protect lives and assets from disasters, aging infrastructure, infectious disease disasters, and public-safety risks.
